text: Great experience. I could tell the devs were trying to make something for a number of play styles with great results. Pros - LOVED the desolate, fantasy world theme. basically zombies, a world lost that I could fight for, survival aspects I could adjust so I could focus more on the story I was experiencing, and loot that progressed with me. - Feeling of open world with sometimes obvious borders and sometimes smooth transitions. - Adjustable difficulty even after creating the world/savegame. This paid off when I learned that my play style demands I explore every corner and a little more time in the shroud was more enjoyable for me. - Level design had me turned around plenty of times requiring me to use paths that were obvious if I was paying attention. I rarely missed something, but sometimes I did so the balance was great for me. - Base building was fun. I ended up taking over a portion of Fort Kelvin and spent time adventuring and took breaks repairing the fort. - Crafting through NPCs so I could leverage their skills rather than need to level up mine. I am adventurer, not a blacksmith, alchemist, carpenter, tailor and creepy crypt keeper.  - Leveling felt balanced, I was never completely overwhelmed but felt which areas were challenging and which I had grown beyond. - Stable game play throughout. Nothing kills the mood more than a game crash. I had none. - Hand crafted world feel. Going with designed levels was key to some great gameplay. - NPCs are like perfect roomates most of the time. They do not eat your food, They unobtrusively show dialog or shout a quick hey at you when they want to say something important. If only they were not oblivious to you being in build mode and standing right where you want to build. Otherwise they leave you alone.  Cons - Liked that there were progressively stronger weapons, but the weapon strength based on weapon level felt like a way to avoid making more content. - Graphical glitches here and there. Some seams broken, stretched textures too. Not enough to complain but enough to mention here. - World is not random so once you've seen it, it will be there the next time around.  - NPCs are missing something. For many they are just tools to be used and they are great for that. But for those that are building a base the NPCs can live in and be protected, it falls short. They are safe without walls. There are no raiding events and spawning is prohibited close to base. I had Vukah wandering a stones throw away from NPCs with a direct line of sight and a walk-able path between them. The NPCs were wandering around like there was no threat nearby. Sometimes they even looked at each other. - Lighting is a bit weird. The sun is not really moving but a shadow is shifting like time is on fast forward. Sometimes the light makes a pixelated appearance on a surface.   For the Devs, Great job. I really enjoyed this. You hit the mark in so many ways. I want more. If there were a way to get a sense of terraforming, like pushing back the shroud near a base, a way to reclaim a part of the world, I would play for so much longer. Not sure why building must be constrained to areas within an altar, but having the world reset everywhere conveniently allows farming materials and gives a sense of repopulation  but also left me with no sense of impact on the world. If it were easy to report broken seams like a pause, click to report a broken seam here button, I would do it. This world looks so good without them. Thank you for this great game.

text: One of My All-Time Favorite Games  Enshrouded has become one of my favorite games I’ve ever played. Disclaimer: I’ve only played it in co-op, so my experience and opinion are based entirely on playing with my wife.  The combination of exploration, survival, building, combat, and RPG progression works incredibly well. There’s always something new to discover, and playing alongside friends makes every adventure feel that much more memorable.  The world is beautiful and mysterious, and I love how naturally the game encourages you to explore. The building system is also fantastic. It’s easy to get completely lost in designing and improving your base, and there’s something incredibly satisfying about seeing it evolve as you progress.  Progression is another huge highlight for me. Finding new gear, unlocking abilities, discovering new areas, and gradually becoming stronger always gives you a reason to keep going. And with at least one friend, even the simple moments, exploring, gathering resources, building, or getting completely sidetracked can turn into some of the best memories.  Enshrouded is one of those games where you can sit down intending to play for an hour and suddenly realize you’ve been playing all night. For me, the co-op experience is where this game really shines.  Highly recommended if you have a friend to play with. It’s easily one of my favorite co-op gaming experiences. Disclaimer: I’ve only played it in co-op, so my experience and opinion are based entirely on playing with my wife.  The combination of exploration, survival, building, combat, and RPG progression works incredibly well. There’s always something new to discover, and playing alongside friends makes every adventure feel that much more memorable.  The world is beautiful and mysterious, and I love how naturally the game encourages you to explore. The building system is also fantastic. It’s easy to get completely lost in designing and improving your base, and there’s something incredibly satisfying about seeing it evolve as you progress.  Progression is another huge highlight for me. Finding new gear, unlocking abilities, discovering new areas, and gradually becoming stronger always gives you a reason to keep going. And with at least one friend, even the simple moments, exploring, gathering resources, building, or getting completely sidetracked can turn into some of the best memories.  Enshrouded is one of those games where you can sit down intending to play for an hour and suddenly realize you’ve been playing all night. For me, the co-op experience is where this game really shines.  Highly recommended if you have a friend to play with. It’s easily one of my favorite co-op gaming experiences. text: I don't think I've ever come across another survival/crafting game that has hooked me for as long as Enshrouded has so far. As of this review, I'm sitting at 70 hours in my current MP playthrough, and we're not even half way through all the current content; and yet I'm not feeling remotely any burnout at all, still.   The game's building system might genuinely be the best of any game out there, and the tech behind how blocks merge their models along with the great lighting system are truly unique and mind-blowing at times. Tie that with the NPC system that gives you a reason to build multiple houses for all your bases' NPCs (if you want!), and you've got what I find to be the best base building in any game.  On the combat and progression side of things, every biome feels extremely unique, along with the sheer amount of new resources you'll discover in each. Armour sets and gear equally feel progressively more visually intriguing and beneficial.  While I usually hate comparing games to others, this is pretty much just Terraria but in 3D (though a fair bit more grounded and consistent with its' themes).  Highly recommend it for absolutely anyone that enjoys the survival/crafting genre, and can't wait to see what 1.0 looks like!

text: 100 Hours Later...  Enshrouded is one of the few survival-crafting games that kept me engaged for over 100 hours.  The exploration is fantastic, the world is beautiful, and the building system is easily one of the best in the survival genre. The freedom to create detailed structures and customize your base is what kept me playing long after completing most of the main content.  Combat and progression are enjoyable, and the developers have done a great job supporting the game with regular updates.  However, there are still areas that could be improved. Late-game combat can become repetitive, enemy variety is somewhat limited, and loot progression could use more depth. As someone who spends a lot of time building, I also wish the game had a free-build camera mode. Constructing large or detailed projects would be much more convenient if builders could move the camera independently without having to position their character every time.  Despite these shortcomings, Enshrouded already offers an impressive amount of content and one of the best building experiences available in a survival RPG.  What I'd like to see in the future:  1. Free-build camera mode 2. More enemy variety 3. Deeper loot and endgame progression 4. More building quality-of-life features

text: I love Enshrouded. I'm so glad I wanted for early access to end, it's a completely different game than when EA first came out. I played 4 hours and logged off, didn't touch it again until now. The fact that it's not overwhelmingly positive is a crime. I'm someone who plays mostly structured games that usually your hand or roguelikes. So in the beginning I uninstalled 3 different times out of frustration. I'm not sure why I kept coming back because I haven't felt like picking a game up in a while, but I'm so glad I did. At first because of my unfamiliarity with this genre, I was playing a long with a lets play from a youtuber that had also never played before. I recommend that to others like me who need a starting "push". Once I was past that stage of "what the heck am I doing" I was beyond happy. This is MY GOTY. I've got a solo run going where I listen to all the lore (everything is VOICED!!) and then the game with him where he likes to skip everything and rush out with his bow in hand cheesing enemies. I prefer the pacing of solo vs Co-Op personally. I like the difficulty difference and the slower pace. It's like a 5 level difference between solo and Co-Op for me. Which if you haven't played, levels take a while to get in solo. I'm at 64 hours and I'm level 15 solo, 10 Co-Op. Co-Op is so much fun though, the magic and laughter we've had playing is a breath of fresh air and I can tell he's really enjoying himself. I love love love battle mage and the fact that I can blend in necromancer. As a necro main I was very happy to at least get a taste of summons. The skill tree is flexible but builds like daggers could be buffed. There's so much room for creativity though. The skill tree is fun and not complicated, you don't need a build guide. Same with gear, I just check for bigger numbers and skills I use and I'm good. It's not POE levels of complicated. I will say that double jump and updraft for glider should be hinted as mandatory because without them I simply don't understand how traversal would be possible. Kinda the same for grappling flying enemies as a pure melee build. If I didn't watch the youtube lets play, I wouldn't have figured that out. The developers did an amazing job with the quest system, the fact that it constantly keeps you on your toes, takes you to the next upgrade or exciting thing, and doesn't feel like a boring mess.. I'm usually spamming through quests on every other game and skipping all side quests possible. But even side quests lead you to chests and exploration. I hate questing normally but on this game I've completed every quest so far. And when you think you've "caught up" ten more quests are given to you, never feeling overwhelmed because it just leads you to discover new things and more awesome loot. Loot in Enshrouded is so fun, I found myself checking everything. In the wild I'd dig up a grave and boom a chest. Open a hidden wall, boom chest. Freaking go in the basement, a chest. Top of a building, a chest. Loot, good loot, everywhere. I caught myself smiling proud of myself a lot when I'd find a chest hidden behind a wall. Big brain energy lol If you find yourself with too many items the game unlocks bigger backpacks and chests as you play. Enshrouded also has smart storage that you unlock over time. With a sorting system of chests and a automatic button to quick stack to near by chests. And farming isn't daunting. You don't have big numbers of resources you need to make a machine (which there are plenty of crafting stations to make) it's like 15 of a mob drop to make said thing. Only "grind" I experienced was when I started with plant fiber. Me and plant fiber where enemies. Now I have stacks of it. Which brings me to actual farming. I love it, it's easy once you figure out how it works. I feel like the devs could've explained it better. Basically you plant seedlings from a grow box on farm soil you use to place via the building tool. Harvest, and repeat just the seedling process. Farming is for potions and food buffs. I always like to keep all my food buffs going. The food buffs are "class based" and for things like stamina. If you are a hybrid build the skill tree actually has a skill that allows you to run multiple buffs at once. There is also pet taming and fishing. The map is huge and moving around the map is easy enough. After a specific quest (no spoilers) you basically open up a whole new region, most games would've stopped right there but it just keeps going and going. Which also leads me to the next thing. Altars. You can have multiple altars built to teleport around as long as it's not in the shroud areas. Altars are limited based on altar level, similar to V-Rising. You start with 3 altars, then five after upgrading, and so on. You can dig out of places if you are lazy like me and don't want to find the path that leads you out lol. Also the gliders and grappling hooks in Enshrouded are actually so worth it. You can actually glide for a very long time. I HATE building which turned me off from picking up Valheim. You do not have to build in this game, but if you choose to man are you spoiled. I'll happily keep my box house, while others can rebuild villages or make their on amazing structures. I don't like puzzles either but they are fairly easy in Enshrouded. I don't have to worry about timers patterns etc, just where is the button, go press said button and find the next button. Get big chest. I suck at reviews but I really wanted to put my vote out there, especially as someone who would usually never play this kind of game. Dang I'm going to be sad when I finally put it down. I'm forever jealous of others who are just going to be starting their adventure with no idea how amazing it's about to be. TL;DR Solo fun, Co Op fun, looting fun, everything fun. Building is easy and only complicated if you want it to be. Puzzles, skill trees, gear, easy to understand and flexible. Map is huge, plenty to explore. Seriously just play. Make sure to put skill points in double jump and updraft. Have fun! :)

text: [b] Enshrouded [/b] is one of those games that can truly surprise you with its quality even in Early Access. The project is developing steadily, and it is clear that the developers have a strong vision. The world is large and full of different biomes, quests, and activities, which makes it hard to feel bored. Exploration is very satisfying, and discovering new areas encourages you to keep playing.  One of the biggest strengths is the variety of the map. Each biome has its own atmosphere and identity, so the gameplay does not become repetitive. The character progression system, building mechanics, and quest design allow you to spend many hours in the game while still feeling a sense of progress. It is engaging and very enjoyable, especially if you like survival games with RPG elements.  However, there is one clear downside, and that is optimization. Even on very powerful hardware, the performance can feel average, and the lack of additional graphics options such as DLSS or frame generation makes it harder to improve smoothness. I hope these are only Early Access issues that will be improved over time.  Despite these technical problems, this is definitely a thumbs up. The potential is huge, and even now the game can provide many hours of great fun.

text: Honestly? It's like Skyrim, to me, on the aspect that it has vast exploration, a lot of interactivity with the world around you (minus the NPCs, they're okay on that part), skill level tree that branches out on how you want your character to turn out, and a lot of good enemies/bosses that it never gets dull. I'm over here having to squint my eyes, or open them wide, to not die from a pitfall, or some spawn of enemies jump scaring me. I turned up my brightness a little, so it kind of helped, but I would prefer some sort of wearable lantern/light source to help with the dark, as I can't hold a torch in one-hand and wield a weapon in the other.

text: A amazing game filled with adventure and potential. I really enjoyed this game as i played. I hope this game continues to grow. I don't know if the game devs are listening but if they are this is what the game needs: 1. More life: for examples more NPCs that are in the world. Maybe add a caravan or a traveling merchant, also more cities filled with survivors  that found a way to survive the horror of the Shroud. Maybe add a function were random people hear about you accomplishment destroying the shrouds roots and want to come to you settlement and if they come there they will could build too and wonder the settlement. 2. Increase the level cap to 100. You reach the level cap too quickly and once you reach it some people don't feel motivated to continue to play.  3. More loot, more loot, more loot. The more loot the better. There is a lot already but as a gamer to the core more is better. It would be nice to be able to go to a random chest and find something no one has found before. As a gamer i want to feel the excitement to find the next thing. Nothing like finding a sword that actual feels like a real treasurer. 4. Mounts. This game would really benefit from this. I would love to find a baby dragon that i can raise that eventual becomes an adult that i can ride. 5. Companions. If your a single player it gets lonely in the Shroud. Can i have a dog, cat, person i saved from the Shroud, and so on. 6. More players in one world. Imagine being able to play with 100 others players. PvP? 7. More decorations for you to discover and build. yes this game has a lot already but it needs more. the more the better. 8. A better character creator. Its okay right now but its super basic. There is more i could add but over all this game is still in the works. The concept so far is amazing, the building is the best that i have ever seen. The potential is there, take that potential and make this game legendary!

text: This game has a lot to offer. There's an incredibly rich story and lots of lore to dig through, there's an effing MASSIVE world to explore with truly a lot to discover in it. The most recent v1.0 update did a lot to diversify the combat and made some great changes but it can still sometimes be tricky. I can't speak to lag issues as I haven't experienced any myself and I'm running an RTX 4060 on high visual settings, with vsync on. I don't have super new monitors either so maybe that helps?   Anyway it's a fantastic game and well worth the money if you're into exploration, character and story development, and massive world diversity.

text: Extremely addictive survival game with enough casual elements to keep things fun without making it feel too stressful. The world is visually beautiful, and even in its current state, Enshrouded already offers a lot to enjoy.  The co-op experience has easily been a 10/10 for me. You can have your own solo world, build and progress at your own pace, then take that same character into a completely different server and enjoy the game with friends without affecting your personal save.  I also really like how quests work in multiplayer. If your friends complete a quest while you're offline, you can still go back later since quest items and bosses respawn. You can complete it yourself, get the XP, and remove it from your quest log.  There are also plenty of optional side quests scattered throughout Embervale through NPCs and lore books. They give you more reasons to explore the cursed lands and discover places you might otherwise miss. Since many of these quests can be completed again, it also works really well for shared servers where someone might join late or miss something.  Overall, Enshrouded mixes survival, exploration, building, quests, and co-op really well. It's one of those games where you can easily lose a few hours without even noticing.  They chased the Elixir... and released the Shroud.  Highly recommended

text: Insane to me that I haven't reviewed the game yet, so let's fix that.  I started playing immediately at the launch of early access and have 700+ hours over 3 worlds.  This game is utterly phenomenal.  One of the best mash-ups of survival, adventure, RPG, crafting, building, etc in the genre.  It's fairly resource-intensive on the PC, but really beautiful if you can run it at max settings.  The only performance issue I've experienced is intermittent crashing (sometimes more than others at different phases of early access, but still occasionally at 1.0 release).  Other than performance, my biggest complaint is the questing system.  It's very difficult to keep the entire party in sync because if you are just slightly out of range you don't get credit for lore notes and some quest advancement steps, and even if you are together when looting a quest objective, you typically have to pass it around the whole group to make sure everyone gets credit.  Just be careful to avoid salvaging anything quest related until you're sure everyone got credit.  Outside that, I've got nothing but good things to say about the game.  One of the best building systems since Minecraft.  Combat has gone through a lot of updates during early access, but I think it's in a pretty good place.  It doesn't reinvent the wheel much, with the classic approaches to melee, ranged and magic, with generous enough skill points that you can pretty much get most if not all of what you want so long as you don't spread your points out too much between the classes.  Honestly, I'd much rather be in game playing it than continuing to write this review.  Unless this isn't the genre for you or you don't think your PC could play it, there's really no reason to NOT jump on board and go on an adventure!  I recommend bringing friends, but it works great solo as well.  I'm always the host in my groups, as I typically had the most powerful PC and internet connection, so I've also been the one typically doing all the grindy stuff (gardening, mining, etc) in-between gaming sessions, so I've gotten fairly decent exposure to playing solo, including farming the Albaneve boss pre-1.0 nerf for it's head for the trophies.  I find it to be well balanced at least for solo and small groups.  So buy it and start playing!

text: I've been lucky to be a part of a consistent playthrough of Valheim with some friends that has spanned the last six months. As that has wound down, we searched for our next game to play on a weekly basis.  We ran across Enshrouded. Which seemed to tick all of our boxes. While also offering a different experience. So we decided to hop in and start a world.  Fast forward two weeks.  The building system has exceeded our expectations and has inspired even our least crafty hunter/explorers to try it out.  The skill tree is nice. You get a noticeable sense of your progression over time.  The resource grind feels balanced.  The hand-crafted world makes looting a blast. I feel like an addict searching every nook and cranny.  The quests are numerous and scattered everywhere. There never seems to be a shortage of things you can go do.  We spent three hours powering our way through a Hollow Hall while severely underleveled. This was one of our pinnacle experiences thus far. Just when we feel like we've got the hang of the puzzles. We encounter the glider section above a poison-covered slide. 10/10. The debrief break after that was unreal, recounting the nonstop combat we had been engaged in. Chain lightning saved the day against hordes multiple times.  I can't wait to explore the world further. It looks like we've still barely scratched the surface of maybe 10% of the map.  Cheers to a remarkable game and the developers behind it! Excited to see where this thing goes.

text: What is this game really? Some weird combination of Elden Ring, Valheim, and World of Warcraft? It seems to work.  Edit to say a little more now that I'm deeper in...  the world is very large, beautiful, and strongly 3-dimensional with huge underground caverns seamlessly integrated. There's a real sense of accomplishment just getting to a new area; navigating the terrain has just the right level of difficulty.  Perhaps the one negative is that the world isn't as interesting as it could be in terms of stuff happening. The post-apocalyptic lore is an excuse for this - but the lore could have been different and there could have been more monster types, more wildlife types, more diverse locations with interesting local events, factions, conflicts, friendly NPCs, etc etc...  Oh and they've got a major exploit where the building system can be used to trivialise any locked door, by dismantling it. text: Review as of Early Access.  There are games that just become great - and this is one that's on that path - and will hopefully stay there. Early Access is just the "thing" now, so you have to be patient with this reality and the constant updates/expansions. That being said, there's currently plenty to do and the multiplayer/co-op is executed very well. Minimal crashes or glitches and they've updated some of the quest progression dynamics. As a VERY long time gamer, I've seen many games come and go - I see this as up there with the likes of Satisfactory, Valheim, Grounded, Fallout, The Forest (first one), Subnautica (both), Green Hell, Conan Exiles and all the "top tier" games survival/co-op/base building. The world is fairly large now with several biomes/areas as well as dungeon areas (Hallow Halls) which can turn into 2, 3 or even 4 hour missions each. Just don't exit a Hallowed Hall before you've completed each Hallowed Hall or you'll lose your progress and have to start it all over again. We learned this after the second hour of progression and stopped to have dinner.   The graphics are beautiful, the game play and combat is satisfying (lots of skill customization, warrior, barbarian, ranger, wizard - many more) - they're still tweaking it - and the base building is nice but still a bit "wonky". The NPC enemies are predictive but change with levels so that adds a bit of challenge (they're tweaking it). Weapons have a great selection with different buffs and attributes. A point of note is that there are several pre-built structures in the game already that can serve as perfectly good "base" areas and I appreciate that since you have a limited amount of Flame Altars you can create for expansion or multi-base purposes. I as many people, set up my main base at the Blue Goblet tavern (you'll find it) since it was nicely laid-out and in good condition with lots of space on 4 levels - basement through attic. Just plop down a flame altar inside or next to it and bingo - instant base build in a fairly central location. It also has enough space for "necessary" farming of plants and food items, but if you want to build a "farm" layout, there's a few flatter areas in the world - just need to build your own structures.   You won't go wrong with this game if you enjoy multiplayer/survival/co-op/base building in the Fantasy Genre with friends. Just note you'll want more and more content as you finish-up the existing quests. A bit more character customization would be welcome - but again, they have a good road map and I'm hopeful they'll keep to it. I especially like the upgrade-able glider feature of the game which makes travel around the world easier and a lot of fun.   All in all depending on what you think of the price I highly recommend playing this game. It's one of the games you think about when you're not playing it - and that says a lot.

text: Really fun survival game. Tons of content and runs very smoothly for an EA game. I think I've reached my end until the next update and wanted to share my thoughts  What I liked: - Building. It was pretty user friendly,  which is big for me because as much as I love doing it in these games, I'm not very good at it. Also, the game doesn't make you gather crazy amount of materials to build. You still have to chop and mine, but I don't feel like it makes you do it to much.  - Exploring. The game is so big already and while there are quest markers telling me what's next, I've had a lot of fun just running and gliding in another direction. This was usually rewarded with finding a village or cave or mine that had some lore to read. No game changing finds, but it felt rewarding to find something new off the beaten path.  - NPCs / Quests. Not something I usually see in this type of game, but I thought it added a fun element to the usual recipe.  - Performance. I played on Steam Deck and it ran great. Ate some battery, but if I tweaked the settings a bit I was getting about two hours with everything still looking and running fine.  - The Shroud. It adds a planning element to exploration. Going in to mine, for a quest, or just exploring new areas means different amounts of time and preparation. There was always a way out, as long as I kept my eye on the time and planned accordingly... which I didn't always do!  Needs Improvement: - Combat. It's not bad, just a little bland. This isn't always a big deal for me in survival games, but the game forces a lot of combat and it gets old to me after a bit. When I jump back in after an update or two, I'll try a different style, I leaned hard in to mage this time.  - Crafting vs Drops. You can either craft weapons and armor or use whqt you find/loot throughout the world. I felt the found items were usually better which diminished the need to craft new weapons, something I like doing in these games.  - Biome diversity. There are different biomes in the game, but I didn't feel a major difference between them as I went from one to the other.  Villages, trees, and the general aesthetic still felt the same.  I think survival fans will like this one and I am excited to see how they progress!

text: This is based on my current run of the game, i did play it at the start of the year when it first came out so i thought i would give it another try to see how things have changed.  I find most of the game pretty decent, but the combat needs a bit of work with blocking as you need to be pixel perfect with it.  Hallow Halls is meant to be for groups, but then why is a NPC locked behind it, what a stupid design choice. It's a huge let down if you're a solo player, as you need to out level the dungeons in order to complete them as they're "designed for groups" which being an open world survival craft is plain stupid. The game isn't bad, but it does have some questionable things going on with it. Stam takes so long to recharge when running around and in combat can cause issue if you get swarmed from mobs.  If the devs fixed a few things up and made the game run a bit better ( hammers the CPU ) then i would absolutely recommend it, until then i would wait and see.  Edit: played again to see what has changed. While some of what i have said has been fixed, melee combat is the worst I've played by far. Dodge rolling you still get hit, parry window is still to small / unreliable, bosses melee attacks follow you and one shot you, it's just cheap and nasty combat and very annoying. swing animations cancelling has a dely on it and defeats the use of it, melee swings roots in place you as well. Melee in this game is just not worth it and doesn't feel good or fair.  1.0 review at around half way into the game: So much i like about the game, then there is melee combat. Devs say it's a skill issue, i say it's a dev skill issue and if you the dev think this is good combat please get out of making games. 2h weapons animations are far too slow and you will be hit during the animation a lot of the time as enemies attack way faster than you. Animation locking is dumb / delay on animation cancel is stupid. It makes the game feel clunky at times.  Projectile lock on is stupid, and the mobs I've come across that have it are the most annoying to fight. You end up 95% of the fight running away and trying to line of sight the projectile.   If you want to play as melee in this game, be prepared for a bad time. . .   Everything else is fine about the game.
